The widths of the confidence intervals (CIs) are primarily influenced by uncertainty and variability in the factors that affect the outcomes over different time horizons. It’s also important to note that outcomes outside the stated intervals, while less likely, are still possible. Specific risks or events could push outcomes beyond these ranges. For example, an unexpected policy announcement, geopolitical event, or major economic shock could drive drastic deviation from expected trends.
